figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of RAG-Audio and two baselines. Given a brain-decoded CLAP embedding 𝑧, direct generation samples from noise and may be dominated by the generator prior; retrieval returns the nearest training clip but is non-generative. RAG-Audio initializes the frozen generator from the exemplar latent 𝑧0 perturbed to an intermediate time, 𝑧𝑡0 , preserving stimulus-related structure while the anchoring strength 𝑠 (with 𝑡0 = 𝑠𝑇) controls the trade-off between faithfulness and novelty.

Figure 2: The RAG-Audio pipeline. The decoder 𝑓𝜃 maps an fMRI response 𝑥 to a CLAP embedding 𝑧; the nearest exemplar 𝑎∗ is retrieved and encoded to 𝑧0, perturbed to an intermediate time 𝑡0 = 𝑠𝑇 (𝑧𝑡0 ), and the frozen generator denoises from 𝑧𝑡0 conditioned on 𝑧 to produce ?̂?. The strength 𝑠 trades faithfulness against novelty.

Table 1: Main comparison on Brain2Music (𝑛=300; 10-way chance 0.10), all methods run in a single harness. Exemplar anchoring lifts identification from 0.14–0.18 (direct) to the retrieval level (0.40–0.43) and cuts FAD by up to ∼10× for AudioLDM and TangoFlux, but not for autoregressive MusicGen.
Figure 3: Decoder localization: voxel relevance scores (red) overlap the Harvard–Oxford auditory-cortex mask (blue), with 78% of top voxels in bilateral superior temporal gyrus.
Figure 4: Ten-way identification versus anchoring strength 𝑠: low 𝑠 stays near the retrieval bound, high 𝑠 decays to the 0.10 chance level; working range 𝑠≈0.25–0.40.
Figure 5: Ten-way identification and FAD per generator: anchoring restores AudioLDM and TangoFlux to retrieval level but not autoregressive MusicGen.
Figure 6: Faithfulness (identification) versus novelty: direct is novel but unfaithful, retrieval faithful but verbatim, RAG-Audio faithful and generative.

Figure 7: Per-genre reconstructions: stimulus, RAG-Audio, and direct generation (log-mel spectrograms). Cyan lines are stimulus onsets (shared per row); the corner box is CLAP similarity to the stimulus (green/orange/red). Direct generation is realistic but off-grid and low-similarity; RAG-Audio recovers onset and harmonic structure (on-grid, high) without copying any retrieved clip. Structural, not sample-accurate, closeness.

Table 2: Identification at 𝑁 =2, 5, 10 for every generator × arm (direct, RAG, retrieval; 𝑛=300, chance 1/𝑁). RAG matches the retrieval bound for the latent-trajectory generators but not MusicGen. †: only 10-way was aggregated for AudioLDM (Table 1).
Figure 9: Genre confusion for the RAG arm (TangoFlux).
